outcome: Length of hospital stay for infants
cohort: Maternal patients with premature rupture of membranes (PROMs) lasting more than 12 hours or meconium-stained amniotic fluid (MSAF), and their infants.
finding: Bacterial growth was observed in 13 out of 30 amniotic fluid samples, with Escherichia coli being the most prevalent (40%), and infants born with PROMs accompanied by MSAF experienced a significantly longer hospital stay (5.5 days) compared to those with PROMs or MSAF alone.
